domains.name: Return Path Structure
domains.point_in_time_availability: Yes — daily bars are available at decision time
domains.expected_economic_mechanism: Two stocks with identical total returns can have fundamentally different paths. A stock that rose steadily has positive momentum with low uncertainty; one that zigzagged has high path volatility suggesting disagreement or mean-reversion pressure. Path structure captures the quality of a price move, not just its magnitude.
domains.overlap_with_tested: LOW — existing features capture levels (ret_10/20/30) and volatility (vol_10/30) but not the temporal structure of the path within a window
domains.implementation_difficulty: LOW — all inputs are OHLCV bars, standard rolling computations
domains.leakage_risk: LOW — all path features use only past data within a trailing window

candidate_features.name: path_max_drawdown_20
candidate_features.formula: max peak-to-trough decline in close prices over trailing 20 sessions

domains.name: Return Asymmetry and Tail Risk
domains.expected_economic_mechanism: Negative skewness in recent returns indicates tail risk — more frequent or larger negative moves. Markets may compensate for tail risk with higher expected returns, or negative skewness may signal ongoing selling pressure that depresses future returns. Either way, asymmetry is information not captured by symmetric measures (mean, std).
domains.overlap_with_tested: LOW — existing features are symmetric (ret_10/20/30, vol_10/30). Skewness and kurtosis are orthogonal moments.
domains.implementation_difficulty: LOW — standard skewness/kurtosis computations on rolling windows

candidate_features.name: return_skew_20
candidate_features.formula: skewness of daily returns over trailing 20 sessions

candidate_features.name: return_kurt_20
candidate_features.formula: excess kurtosis of daily returns over trailing 20 sessions

domains.name: Volatility Dynamics
domains.expected_economic_mechanism: Volatility is not static. A stock transitioning from low to high volatility is in a different regime than one with stable high volatility. The stability of volatility itself (vol-of-vol) and the direction of vol change carry information about regime transitions that vol levels miss.
domains.overlap_with_tested: MEDIUM — vol_ratio_10_30 captures some regime info. But vol-of-vol (stability of vol) and vol change rate are genuinely new.
domains.implementation_difficulty: LOW-MEDIUM — requires nested rolling computations (vol of vol)

candidate_features.name: vol_of_vol_20
candidate_features.formula: std(rolling_std(daily_return, 5), 20) — volatility of 5-day rolling volatility over 20 days

candidate_features.name: vol_change_20
candidate_features.formula: vol_10(D-1) - vol_10(D-20) — change in short-term volatility over 20 days

domains.name: Macro Regime Conditioning
domains.information_source: FRED data (DS-000003): CPI, DFF (Fed Funds Rate), UNRATE (Unemployment Rate)
domains.historical_availability: CPI: 1947-present. DFF: 1954-present. UNRATE: 1948-present. All well before our stock data start (1996).
domains.point_in_time_availability: Yes, with publication lags: CPI ~2-3 weeks, DFF real-time, UNRATE ~1-2 weeks. Using published values respects PIT.
domains.coverage: Macroeconomic — applies to all instruments uniformly
domains.expected_economic_mechanism: Macro conditions (rate environment, inflation, labor market) change the regime in which all stock-level signals operate. A momentum signal may work differently in a rising-rate vs falling-rate environment. Macro features condition the interpretation of stock-level features.
domains.overlap_with_tested: NONE — no existing feature uses macro data
domains.implementation_difficulty: LOW — monthly/quarterly series merged to daily frequency via last-available observation
domains.leakage_risk: LOW — macro data published with known lags; using published values respects PIT

candidate_features.name: macro_dff_level
candidate_features.formula: Current Fed Funds Rate (daily, last available observation)

candidate_features.name: macro_dff_change_3m
candidate_features.formula: DFF(D) - DFF(D-63) — change in Fed Funds Rate over trailing 3 months

domains.name: Autocorrelation Structure
domains.expected_economic_mechanism: First-order autocorrelation captures whether returns exhibit momentum (positive autocorrelation) or mean-reversion (negative autocorrelation) at short horizons.
domains.overlap_with_tested: HIGH — autocorrelation is closely related to momentum features already tested

candidate_features.name: return_autocorr_20
candidate_features.formula: autocorrelation of daily returns at lag 1 over trailing 20 sessions

domains.name: Cross-Asset Relationships
domains.historical_availability: Full history for SPY and all universes
domains.coverage: Requires benchmark — limited to instruments with SPY relationship
domains.expected_economic_mechanism: Changes in beta, correlation with market, co-movement regimes. Beta changes may signal regime transitions.
domains.overlap_with_tested: PARTIALLY — sector features exist (Phase 12A) but are simple means/stds. Dynamic beta/correlation is new.
domains.implementation_difficulty: MEDIUM — requires rolling regression or rolling correlation

candidate_features.name: rolling_beta_20
candidate_features.formula: OLS beta of instrument return on SPY return over trailing 20 sessions

candidate_features.name: rolling_corr_20
candidate_features.formula: Pearson correlation of instrument return with SPY return over trailing 20 sessions

summary.highest_novelty: DOM-4 (Macro Regime) — no existing feature uses macro data
summary.lowest_implementation_difficulty: DOM-1 (Path Structure), DOM-2 (Asymmetry) — standard rolling computations on existing OHLCV
